title: Modernizing critical security infrastructure
summary: A Check Point gateway refresh, with high availability and change validation at the center.
context: Enterprise firewall modernization for a banking environment, delivered through my security engineering engagement at Etech International.
work: Supported a Check Point 5600 HA to 9700 gateway refresh and management upgrades.
Validated cluster health, synchronization, Secure Internal Communication and policy installation.
Participated in failover testing, staged hotfix maintenance and post-change verification.
Documented changes and verification results for operational handover.
outcome: The refreshed platform was brought into operation with failover validation and documented follow-up maintenance.
takeaway: A migration is only complete when the system is observable, recoverable and ready for the team that will operate it.

title: A private AI workspace for internal teams

context: An internal AI infrastructure initiative alongside my systems and DevOps work at Chez Inspheris / Lively Software.
work: Set up and tuned GPU-backed model serving and containerized AI components.
Connected a browser-based AI interface with private inference services.
Configured role-specific Hermes profiles and repository-based workflows.
Worked on reverse-proxy access, Markdown publishing and cross-profile validation.
outcome: Internal model-serving and agent workflows supported practical experimentation and team-specific use cases.
takeaway: Useful AI infrastructure needs the same attention to access, operations and documentation as any other internal service.

title: Making infrastructure easier to operate
summary: Monitoring, alerting and backup visibility for the services teams depend on.
context: Day-to-day production infrastructure operations, spanning virtual machines, application services and backup systems.

Investigated operational incidents across Linux, web services and databases.
outcome: Operational visibility connects service health, resource usage and recovery information in the daily support workflow.
takeaway: A useful dashboard helps an engineer decide what to do next.

title: From source control to repeatable releases
summary: Jenkins pipelines and Git-based workflows for production application delivery.
context: Release and infrastructure support for SaaS and intranet applications at Chez Inspheris / Lively Software.
work: Built and maintained Jenkins CI/CD pipelines and Git workflows.
Supported containerized services and application deployment steps.
Maintained reverse proxies and Java / Tomcat application services.
Troubleshot releases alongside application and infrastructure teams.
outcome: Repeatable delivery workflows support application releases and day-to-day production operations.
takeaway: Automation works best when a release is understandable, traceable and straightforward to troubleshoot.
